verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct [1][2]. The task required three coupled functions in `/app/solution.py` implementing Fourier-domain beam propagation, ABCD-matrix waist tracking through a lens system, and a combined transmission routine that finds the post-lens focus and intensity field [3]. The agent did write all three functions and declared completion [4][11], but its physics diverges materially from the reference on every sub-step: `propagate_gaussian_beam` uses a paraxial Fresnel filter `exp(-iπλz(fx²+fy²))` with unshifted FFTs instead of the reference angular-spectrum propagator with `fftshift`/`ifftshift` and a `sqrt((1/λ)²-fx²-fy²)` transfer function, causing the hidden 28.1 energy-conservation `np.allclose` on integrated power to fail [5][8]; `gaussian_beam_through_lens` explicitly ignores `L1` and applies only `Mz·Mf1·Ms` ABCD chaining, whereas the reference partitions the axis at `L1` and uses distinct q-parameter formulas before and after the lens, so the hidden 28.2 waist-array comparison also fails [6][7][9]; and `Gussian_Lens_transmission` inherits those upstream errors and squares the z=0 propagated amplitude rather than returning the reference Gaussian intensity profile at the argmin waist, so the hidden 28.3 tuple comparison fails as well [10][2]. The agent relied on shape checks and toy smoke tests that never compared against conserved-energy or reference values [11][12], while the hidden reference solution implements the angular-spectrum propagator, L1-partitioned waist model, and direct Gaussian focus intensity the tests target [13]. No verifier or harness fault is evident.
